To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FSH and isoproterenol increase cAMP-PDE mRNA, protein, and activity in the rat Sertolli cell.
the Sertoli cells contain a cAMP-PDE that is induced by hormones and is similar to the PDE4D isozyme.
a cAMP phosphodieterase is regulated by hormones in the immature rat testis, and that the cAMP phosphodietersase is regulated by FSH and beta adrenergic agonist in the immature rat tests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of cyclic AMP (cAMP)-phosphodiesterase (PDE) in rat Sertoli cells.
the identification of a hormone inducible form of cAMP PDE in the Sertoi cell.
the regulation of cAMP phosphodieterase (PDE) activity in the Sertol cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cAMP-Pde in rat Sertoli cells is an enzyme of the PDE4 family.
a high-affinity cAMP phosphodi-esterase is present in Sertoli cells, and that this enzyme can be induced by FSH and by beta-adrenergics, but not by cAMP itself.
a PDE4 isoenzyme is the FSH- and beta-adrenerigic agonist-inducible form of the Sertol cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FSH regulates a PDE4 isoform in the Sertolli cell, and the PDE4 isoforms are regulated at the level of gene expression.
the rat Sertoil cell expresses a PDE4B protein, which is a high affinity c-AMP PDE that can be induced by FSH and beta adrenergic agonist.
the Sertoli cells contain at least three distinct cAMP-PDEs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sertoli cAMP-PDE4D5 is a novel, hormone-regulated PDE that is a target for FSH and beta-agonists and may be a key mediator of the FSH-induced increase in cAMP levels in the Sertolli cell.
the Sertoli cells have the ability to regulate their own cAMP levels by producing a high affinity cGMP-PDE.
the PDE4D isoform is the predominant isoform expressed in the rat Sertolli cells.
